trajectory.thought: The leader is a seeded baseline (DBA) and the runner-up margin is statistically indistinguishable. All subset pools performed worse than the full pool, the ranking is unstable, and error correlation is high (0.843) — meaning most models carry similar error and there's little to gain from selective weighting. The stopping rule for a seed leader with an indistinguishable verdict applies here.

action_args.justification: The series is trend-dominated (strength 0.72) with weak seasonality (0.12) and non-stationary. Model ranking is unstable (Kendall tau -0.115) and error correlation is high (mean 0.843, only 2 independent groups), so no subset or fitted weighting can reliably exploit model differences. DBA (DTW barycenter of the full pool) is a robust aggregation that respects the shape of each forecast rather than just averaging levels, which suits a strongly trending series where level errors dominate. All subset-pool baselines scored worse, confirming that the full pool is preferable. The runner-up margin is statistically indistinguishable, so accepting the seed leader is the right call.
